body:
## Problem

After the video decoder's normal drain-to-EOS boundary, `MediaSession` continues owning its final compressed recovery GOP while the session stays alive at EOF. The recovery buffer admits up to 512 packets and 32 MiB of payload, but previously released that final GOP only on a later seek, stop, or destruction.

## Change

- Run the existing decoder drain inside `VideoRecoveryPacketBuffer.retireAfterSuccessfulDrain`, then retire the recovery references before queuing the video EOS marker.
- Preserve replay on thrown drain errors and cancellation.
- Check the generation under the existing buffer lock so an old drain cannot clear a newer seek's GOP. The drain itself runs outside the lock.
- Keep independent Swift/native packet owners valid through their existing reference counts.
- Add focused lifetime regressions, a real-session EOF test, a frozen-baseline ownership experiment, and CI qualification.

“Successful drain” preserves the player's existing normal-return contract; this change does not reinterpret FFmpeg EOF/EAGAIN or tolerated software errors.

## Measured result

The [completed portable ownership job](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/actions/runs/40639152416/job/122652965238) compiled the **exact baseline and candidate packet-owner source** against the repository's verified **FFmpeg 8.1.2**, using **Swift 6.4.1 / Ubuntu 24.04**.

| Final recovery GOP | Payload retained after drain: baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 4 packets / 4 KiB | 4,096 bytes | 0 bytes |
| 16 packets / 1 MiB | 1,048,576 bytes | 0 bytes |
| 512 packets / 32 MiB | 33,554,432 bytes | 0 bytes |

Real `AVBuffer` free callbacks verify that payloads survive during drain, release afterward, and free exactly once. Error, throwing cancellation, stale-generation, seek-during-drain, independent native-clone, and fresh-GOP controls passed.

**48 checks passed for each of baseline/candidate in debug/release** (192 check executions). Debug and release observations agreed. The measured production owner has the same source hash in the later test additions.

These are controlled retained-payload measurements with the recovery buffer as sole owner. They are **not player RSS, decoder/renderer memory, or a CPU-time claim**. Another native owner can legitimately retain a payload after this cache lets go.

## Validation status

- **Passed:** exact-source ownership comparison in debug/release, all six lifecycle controls, baseline/source/native-library provenance checks, Python/YAML parsing, and whitespace checks.
- **Pending CI:** the subsequently added unchanged repository lifetime suite in an isolated Linux package (10 test functions / 12 cases per configuration, debug and release).
- **Pending macOS CI:** compile the actual application graph and run lifetime, packet-ownership, and buffer regressions. A required generated H.264 fixture exercises the real `MediaSession` EOF path: 48 packets, one GOP, 48 submitted frames, and zero observed packet owners before stopping the still-live session.
- Live UI, visible presentation, physical-device playback, and whole-process footprint remain unqualified.

This PR is a **draft while the final regression and native integration gates are pending**. Follow the [current PR checks](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/pull/175/checks) for their status.

## Research and reproduction

[Study, commands, and limitations](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/blob/perf/video-recovery-gop-eof-20261028-bc446/Benchmarks/VideoRecoveryPacketLifetime/README.md) · [Committed raw evidence and receipts](https://github.com/Jagalite/illiquid/tree/perf/video-recovery-gop-eof-20261028-bc446/Benchmarks/VideoRecoveryPacketLifetime/evidence/ubuntu)

Hosted runners explicitly record that the shared Kyoto queue is unavailable and build serially in isolated checkouts. The reproduction instructions preserve the repository's requirement to use Kyoto when it is available.
title: perf: release the final video recovery GOP after decoder drain
